answer: A amateur radio licence with callsign logbook history works as the gate: a callsign logged on the air for years. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. Each of 396 aliases needs its own logbook histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A lantern marker runs through the scheme: every claim is checkable, every fake pays separately, and the nadir ledger turns 396 aliases into 396 bills while the ocean path for the honest stays a single payment.
